title: Trading Policy

tiers.name: Directors and employees
tiers.description: All Directors and employees of the Company. Bound by the whole policy without differentiation, except that clearance for dealing outside or during a blackout period is obtained from the Chairman (or his delegate Director).

tiers.name: Chairman
tiers.description: Distinguished only for clearance: notification or consent for the Chairman's own dealing is obtained from the Lead Independent Director instead of the Chairman.

tiers.name: Related parties
tiers.description: Related parties of Directors and employees as defined in AASB 124: spouses, de facto spouses, dependants under 18, or any other party over whom the Director or employee is deemed to have significant control. The Director or employee must ensure related-party trading does not occur during a blackout period.

exemption_authority: The Chairman (or his delegate Director), or the Lead Independent Director for the Chairman, may give written consent to deal during a blackout period only in exceptional circumstances, and 'will generally be refused unless exceptional circumstances exist' (e.g. severe financial hardship or a court order requiring sale of the shares). No exemption or waiver process is identified for the outright bans on short-term dealing, short selling, or using Company securities as security for margin lending or other loans.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The policy governs 'dealing in the Company's shares' and use of 'the Company's securities as security'; it contains no defined 'Dealing' term and never mentions derivatives, options, swaps or hedging.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: There is no textual basis to determine whether an OTC put/call collar over CIN shares is caught by the policy at all; the safest assumption is that it would be treated as within the spirit of the blackout and margin-lending rules, but this is not addressed.

bespoke_clauses.topic: unqualified ban on shares as loan security
bespoke_clauses.clause: Directors and employees are prohibited from using the Company's securities as security for margin lending arrangements or other loans.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: This is an outright, unqualified prohibition on encumbering CIN shares for any loan, with no Board approval carve-out, exemption authority or waiver process identified anywhere in the policy - fatal to the loan leg of a funded collar.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Should a Director also be a Director of an investee entity, where the holding in that entity exceeds 10% of the Company's total portfolio holding by market value, that Director should also consider the Trading Policy of the investee entity as if it related to shares in the Company.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: As CIN is an investment company, a director dealing in (or collaring) shares of a greater-than-10%-of-portfolio investee must separately comply with that investee's own, potentially different, trading policy.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Such requests, which must be in writing, will generally be refused unless exceptional circumstances exist.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Entering into or unwinding a collar during any of the four blackout periods is presumptively refused; only severe financial hardship or a court-ordered sale are given as examples of sufficient exceptional circumstances.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The Company Secretary is to lodge an Appendix 3Y - Change of Director's Interest Notice with the ASX detailing whether a trade occurred during a closed period where prior written clearance was required and, if prior written clearance was required, whether that clearance was provided and the date on which it was provided.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Any dealing connected to the collar by a director is publicly disclosed together with whether blackout clearance applied and was granted, and the date of that clearance.

summary: A funded collar cannot proceed under this policy because the loan leg is categorically barred: directors and employees are unconditionally prohibited from using Company securities as security for margin lending arrangements or other loans, and no exception, Board waiver or approval pathway for this prohibition appears anywhere in the two-page policy. Short-term dealing and short selling of CIN securities are also flatly banned, which is relevant if the put leg were characterised as a short position, but the policy never mentions derivatives, options, hedging or OTC products at all, so how (or whether) the derivative legs themselves would be treated is genuinely unaddressed. Any dealing in CIN shares outside the recurring blackout periods (monthly NTA release, half-year and full-year results, and the pre-AGM period) requires prior written notification to the Chairman (or the Lead Independent Director for the Chairman's own dealing), while dealing during a blackout period requires prior written consent that 'will generally be refused' absent severe financial hardship or a court-ordered sale. A director who also sits on the board of an investee entity representing over 10% of CIN's portfolio must additionally comply with that entity's own trading policy. Overall verdict: not possible - the express, unqualified ban on encumbering CIN shares for any loan defeats the funded structure regardless of how the derivative legs are analysed.
